criterion 1.description: Calculates US population in 2032 as 358,710,351 (acceptable value is 358,710,351)
criterion 1.justification: From US Population Census by State.csv Find the CAGR based on 2020 through 2024 (columns B through F) for each state (column A). Then apply that CAGR for 8 years (2032 minus 2024) to find the population for that given state. Finally sum up all the states to find the population of 358,710,350.6 --> round to nearest whole number 358,710,351 As an example, Alabama CAGR is 0.61% [=(5,157,699/5,033,094)^(1/4)-1 = 0.006132639] based on Alabama 2020-2024 population. Thus, Alabama 2032 population is 2024 population (5,157,699) multiplied by (1 + 0.61%)^8

criterion 2.description: Calculates total interested people in this genre of toy products in US in 2032 as 53,806,553 (acceptable range is 53,806,552 to 53,806,554)
criterion 2.justification: Using the US population in 2032 from criterion ID 12412 (358,710,350.6 before final rounding), divide by four to get equal age segments: 358,710,350.6 / 4 = 89,677,587.65. Apply the interest rates 25%, 20%, 10%, and 5% to each segment and sum: (0.25 + 0.20 + 0.10 + 0.05) × 89,677,587.65 = 53,806,552.59. Round to the nearest whole number: 53,806,553.

criterion 3.description: Calculates TAM in US in 2032 as $2,690,327,629 (acceptable value of $2,690,327,629)
criterion 3.justification: Using the unrounded total interested people from criterion ID 12413 (53,806,552.59), multiply by $50 per person: 53,806,552.59 × 50 = $2,690,327,629.50. Round to the nearest whole dollar: $2,690,327,629.

criterion 4.description: Calculates SAM in US in 2032 as $269,032,763 (acceptable value of $269,032,763)
criterion 4.justification: Using the unrounded TAM from criterion ID 12414 ($2,690,327,629.50), apply 10% capture: 0.10 × $2,690,327,629.50 = $269,032,762.95. Round to the nearest whole dollar: $269,032,763.

criterion 5.description: Highlights one or more of the following as a risk in the assumptions that may be over-optimistic: - Underestimation of how difficult it would be taking 10% market share from a dominant player like Lego - Sustainability of a $50 spend for toys in a potential downturn - The equal population distribution in the United States among the different age groups
criterion 5.justification: Many of the assumptions may be over-optimistic - $50 per person may be high if economic downturn in 2032 - 10% market share from a dominant player like Lego might be difficult - 25% of people between 0-20 interested in Lego-type products is high

criterion 6.description: Calculates the US population in 2024 as 340,110,988 (acceptable answer of 340,110,988)
criterion 6.justification: From US Population Census by State.csv Sum up the 2024 column (column F) to get 340,110,988 for the US population in 2024. No rounding is required given that the data is already in whole units.
